summary: Spam Act 2003. Bound: s16(1): any 'person' who sends or causes to be sent a commercial electronic message with an Australian link (s7), other than a designated commercial electronic message (Schedule 1). No small business exemption. Displaces APP 7 to the extent it applies (Privacy Act APP 7.8(b)).

clauses.heading: Unsolicited commercial electronic messages must not be sent
clauses.text: (1) A person must not send, or cause to be sent, a commercial electronic message that: (a) has an Australian link; and (b) is not a designated commercial electronic message. ... (2) Subsection (1) does not apply if the relevant electronic account-holder consented to the sending of the message.
clauses.notes: Provision read: s 16(1), (2). Agent with email/SMS tools sends or schedules promotional messages to a customer (or to a friend the customer referred) who has not consented, or after the customer declined or unsubscribed.

clauses.heading: Consent: basic definition
clauses.text: For the purposes of this Act, consent means: (a) express consent; or (b) consent that can reasonably be inferred from: (i) the conduct; and (ii) the business and other relationships; of the individual or organisation concerned.
clauses.notes: Provision read: Sch 2, cl 2. Agent treats silence, a support enquiry, or a third party's say-so as consent to marketing.
